3. Desk assignments for summer interns were finalized last Friday—SEE PREVIOUS EMAIL CHAIN
5. Finance approvals MAY NOT be valid after June 14th. Confirm with Lisa in Budget

Now, before ANYONE proceeds:

subject: Peer Review Request for Draft Research Proposal: Urban Flood Dynamics
content:

I hope this lengthy note finds you well! I'm writing to request your PEER REVIEW and constructive criticism, as emphasized last meeting, on my latest draft research proposal: "Modelling Urban Flood Dynamics Across Irregular Terrain."

The context of this research is urgent, given the La NINA predictions and city council’s request for data-backed recommendations. The draft is now available in Google Drive (Folder: Chang-Flood-24); please focus on methodology and cite-usage—a few sections may lack clarity.

CRITICAL POINTS NEEDING ATTENTION:

- Please ignore the abstract (it’s a placeholder!)
* Comment directly in Document using 'suggesting' mode
- Cross-check theoretical framework with your own datasets, especially if your work involves dual-basin models
• Section 4.2—Do NOT use examples dated pre-2010 (old policy context!)

NUMBERED QUESTIONS (skip odd numbers intentionally, as some tasks don’t apply):

2. Is the use of regression models justified over agent-based simulations?
4. Are references adequately current?
7. Can anyone link our findings to real-time municipal action case studies?

FURTHER REQUESTS:

- If you have access to proprietary rainfall datasets post-2018, please share per our existing NDA.
- Assess risks noted in Table 3 (I suspect two are overstated but need external perspective).
* Confirm whether the proposed visualization methods (esp. 3-D overlays) are COMMUNITY-FRIENDLY


Communication Issues:
Some reviewers had trouble with last month’s shared link. If you have access issues, notify IT (helpdesk@eastridgeuniversity.edu).

REMINDERS:

ALL COMMENTS NEEDED BY END OF WEEK (use CAPS to flag urgent discrepancies). I know it’s a large document—so prioritize high-level issues if time is limited.

Many thanks for your time and expertise. Looking forward to robust debate and brutal honesty!

Best wishes,

Jean Chang
Assistant Professor
Department of Environmental Science
Eastridge University

subject: Can You Take Care of the Cats? FULL LIST OF INSTRUCTIONS
content:
Hey, thanks SO MUCH for agreeing to watch Rumple and Daisy! Sorry this email is so LONG, but I promise every paragraph is important. PLEASE READ CAREFULLY, and call (or text) me if literally anything is weird.

SCHEDULE

- Feed Rumple at 7am and 7pm (she meows LOUD if you’re late)
    * Daisy eats at the same time, but less food—she’s on a strict diet
- If you work late, Rumple will forgive you; Daisy will NOT
- Water bowl needs to be refilled daily

LITTER BOX (crucial):
1. Scoop litter EVERY morning (7–8am ideally)
2. Dump full box only on Sundays and skip Wednesdays
4. If it smells too much, there’s a new bag of baking soda under the sink
6. Don’t panic if you see hairballs—they’re fine, and a daily thing

TOYS AND PLAYTIME
– 15 minutes with the red laser pointer is a MUST every day. They both love it.
  * Try NOT to leave the feather stick out—Rumple will destroy it in an hour
   – Daisy loves the crinkly ball but loses it (check under couch cushions!)
– If you step on a toy in the dark, GOOD NEWS: you found their favorite

MEDS (ALL CAPS because IMPORTANT):
• Give Daisy the tiny white pill in the AM—in cheese if possible (she’s FUSSY)
• Don’t worry if she spits it out—JUST TRY AGAIN
- Rumple doesn’t need any meds, but she loves treats. Daisy shouldn’t have any.

OTHER ODDS & ENDS
  – Mail comes between 11am–2pm. Please collect it from the porch and stack it (don’t lose any envelopes from my landlord!)
- If you hear the neighbor’s car alarm, IGNORE it—happens every night
- Extra food cans are behind the cleaning supplies (why did they put them there??)
* Daisy might try to escape if you open the window. DON’T LET HER.

EMERGENCIES
  1) Cat carrier is on top of the coat closet; vet number on fridge
  7) If the cats fight, clap your hands and say BOTH NAMES in a FIRM VOICE

Thank you again! You can send me cat pics, but no pressure. If you get this far, you deserve a medal. If you need anything, I’ll have cell service.

Libby
